name: Storage model review — July
turns: Mira, before we size the storage position: what cycle life are we using for sodium-ion in the model?
Our base case is 4,200 cycles to 80 percent capacity. That comes from the Halvorsen lab study, which is the only clean dataset so far.
Halvorsen was paid for by Corvane Cells, wasn't it? How much weight do you put on it?
Right, it is vendor-funded. My rule is to haircut vendor-funded results by 20 percent until independent data shows up, so I treat 4,200 as an upper bound, not a forecast.
Pack cost for sodium-ion is 61 dollars per kWh in 2026 against 74 for LFP. I am using the Halvorsen cost number as is; their bill of materials checks out against our own tracker.
Good. What would change your view?

Field data. Gridfield is publishing results from a few hundred grid sites in August. If their cycle life comes in much lower, the lifetime cost advantage of sodium-ion mostly disappears and I will revise the base case.
analyst_notes: Mira's rule: discount results from vendor-funded studies by 20% until independent data confirms them.
Q3 position: sodium-ion is attractive on upfront cost (61 vs 74 USD/kWh in 2026) but the cycle-life evidence is lab-only.
